# Every maximal symmetric-overlap center can fail the sharp bound

This is a counterexample to the proposed selector, not to Oertel's conjecture. It fails already in the continuous planar setting and therefore also for a two-fiber mixed-integer product.

## The polygon and its overlap maximizer

Let

`K=conv{(-4,-3),(4,4),(2,3),(-3,0)}⊂R²`.

The listed vertices are counterclockwise, and `area(K)=9`. Equivalently, its four lower halfplane inequalities are

```
-7x+8y >= 4,
 x-2y  >= -4,
3x-5y  >= -9,
3x-y   >= -9.
```

Define `R_K(s,t)=area(K∩(2(s,t)−K))`. Its unique maximizer is

`c=(-182/233,123/233)`,

with `R_K(c)=1440/233`.

Here is a full exact certificate of maximality and uniqueness. Write the four normals and right-hand sides above as `(n_i,b_i)`, in order, and write `L_i` for `n_i·w=b_i` and `U_i` for `n_i·w=2n_i·(s,t)−b_i`. Near `c`, the intersection polygon has the following active vertex pairs, in counterclockwise order:

```
(U0,L3), (U1,L3), (U1,U2), (L0,U2),
(L0,U3), (L1,U3), (L1,L2), (U0,L2).
```

Solving those pairs gives the affine vertex formulas

```
((-76-14s+16t)/17, (-75-42s+48t)/17)
((-22- 2s+ 4t)/ 5, (-21- 6s+12t)/ 5)
(2s-2,             2t-3)
((-92-48s+80t)/11, (-75-42s+70t)/11)
(( 76+48s-16t)/17, ( 75+42s-14t)/17)
(( 22+12s- 4t)/ 5, ( 21+ 6s- 2t)/ 5)
(2,                 3)
(( 92+70s-80t)/11, ( 75+42s-48t)/11).
```

At `c`, each vertex satisfies exactly its two active constraints. All other constraint slacks are strictly positive; the smallest is `12/233`. Thus these formulas describe the actual intersection polygon on an open neighborhood of `c`, not just at a sampled point. The exact verifier additionally enumerates every pair of constraints and verifies that these are all feasible intersections.

The shoelace formula now gives the local polynomial

`R_K(s,t)=[-9516s²+21644st-13864t²-26292s+31544t-12816]/935`.

Its gradient vanishes at `c`. Its first quadratic coefficient is negative and its Hessian determinant is `3728/55>0`; hence the Hessian is negative definite. In particular, `c` is a strict local maximum.

To prove global maximality, set `D_a=K∩(2a−K)`. Convexity gives

`(1-λ)D_a+λD_b ⊂ D_((1-λ)a+λb)`.

Indeed, both each point and its reflection about the corresponding interpolated center are convex combinations of points of `K`. Brunn–Minkowski therefore makes `R_K^(1/2)` concave on `K`. The vanishing gradient at its positive interior point `c` implies global maximality. If there were a second maximizer, concavity would make every point on the segment between the two a maximizer, contradicting the strict local maximum at `c`. Thus the maximizer is unique.

## Its centroid-type depth bound fails

The closed halfplane

`H={3x-y >= -669/233}`

has `c` on its boundary. It cuts from `K` the quadrilateral with vertices

```
(-260/233,-111/233), (4,4), (2,3), (-104/233,357/233).
```

Its area is `210855/54289`, so

`area(K∩H)/area(K)=70285/162867 < 4/9`.

Thus the unique symmetric-overlap maximizer is not a Grünbaum point with the sharp planar constant.

## Two-fiber mixed-integer version

Set `C=[0,1]×K⊂R×R²`. It is a convex body, and its induced mixed-integer set is `S={0,1}×K`, with total mixed volume `18`.

For a center `(z,a)∈S`, only the same integer fiber contributes to `S∩(2(z,a)−S)`: reflecting the other integer fiber produces index `-1` or `2`, absent from `S`. Therefore its mixed overlap is exactly `R_K(a)`. The only global maximizing centers are `(0,c)` and `(1,c)`.

For `(0,c)`, use the closed ambient halfspace

`H0={3x-y-100z >= -669/233}`.

It contains `(0,c)` and excludes the entire fiber at `z=1`. For `(1,c)`, use

`H1={3x-y+100z >= 100-669/233}`.

It contains `(1,c)` and excludes the entire fiber at `z=0`. The retained cap in the selected fiber is exactly the planar cap above. Each normalized mixed cap mass is consequently

`70285/325734 < 2/9`,

with exact positive gap `6301/977202`. Since `2/9=2^(-1)γ_2`, every maximizer of the mixed symmetric-overlap objective fails the required constant.

The stand-alone script `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_overlap_selector.py` verifies all polygon, active-set, polynomial, derivative, area, and strict-inequality calculations using exact rational arithmetic only.
